$comment: Every repository variable and secret the workflows are allowed to reference.
Names and purposes only — no values, and nothing here is a credential.
It exists because GitHub resolves an unknown secrets.* or vars.* reference to
an empty string instead of failing. A renamed or mistyped name therefore
produces a workflow that runs, succeeds, and does the wrong thing quietly.
That has already happened twice here: secrets.GITHUB_DISPATCH_TOKEN, a name
GitHub refuses to store, and the three read-only Terraform plan credentials.
scripts/check-workflow-config.ts holds this file and .github/workflows/ to
each other, so neither can drift without CI saying so.
required=false means the workflows work without it. Every such entry says
what happens when it is unset, and every reference to one carries its
fallback inline, so an empty value is always a decision rather than an

AMPLITUDE_API_KEY.purpose: Amplitude browser ingestion key, inlined into the site bundle and used by the Worker to scope its analytics relay. Public by construction, which is why it is a variable and not a secret.
AMPLITUDE_API_KEY.whenUnset: The site ships with no analytics at all — the init call is eliminated as dead code and the SDK never reaches the bundle. The Pages workflow warns, because the outcome is otherwise indistinguishable from working analytics.

AMPLITUDE_SERVER_URL.purpose: Worker endpoint the browser falls back to when a privacy extension or network block rejects the direct Amplitude request.
AMPLITUDE_SERVER_URL.whenUnset: Only direct Amplitude ingestion is attempted; a blocked request is simply lost.

CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID.purpose: Account owning the R2 buckets and the Worker. Also the host part of every R2 S3 endpoint URL, and of the Workers AI endpoint the contact check calls.

CONTACT_WORKFLOW_FILE.purpose: Workflow file the Worker dispatches to check a contact-form message before it is forwarded.
CONTACT_WORKFLOW_FILE.whenUnset: Falls back to validate-contact.yml at the reference site.

CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID.purpose: Zone hosting the root domain, where Terraform writes DNS records and the cache ruleset.

CONTENT_BASE_URL.purpose: Public base URL of the content bucket. Both the Pages build and the Worker deploy fetch the published profile from it before they can build anything.

MEDIA_BASE_URL.purpose: Public base URL of the media bucket. The site renders photos from it and the media pipeline builds the record's image links from it.

MEDIA_WORKFLOW_FILE.purpose: Workflow file the Worker dispatches to sanitise a draft's media.
MEDIA_WORKFLOW_FILE.whenUnset: Falls back to process-media.yml at the reference site.

PAGES_BASE_PATH.purpose: Vite base path for the built site.
PAGES_BASE_PATH.whenUnset: Falls back to the project-pages subpath /<repo>/ at the reference site. Set it to / when serving from a custom domain.

PAGES_OWNER.purpose: GitHub user or organisation owning the Pages site; the CNAME for a subdomain site targets <owner>.github.io. Deliberately not GITHUB_PAGES_OWNER — GitHub reserves the GITHUB_ prefix and refuses to store a variable using it, so that name could never have held a value.
PAGES_OWNER.whenUnset: Matches the Terraform default. Only valid while the site is served from the apex, where A and AAAA records are used and no CNAME exists — Terraform's precondition rejects an unset owner alongside a set SITE_SUBDOMAIN.

PAGES_CUSTOM_DOMAIN.purpose: Custom domain written into the Pages artifact as a CNAME file, because Pages otherwise drops the domain on some deploys.
PAGES_CUSTOM_DOMAIN.whenUnset: No CNAME file is written and the site is served from its github.io URL.

PROJECT_SLUG.purpose: Identifier every bucket name is derived from, and the prefix separating this project's Terraform state from any other in the same bucket.

ROOT_DOMAIN.purpose: Registered domain the public hostnames hang off.

SITE_BASE_URL.purpose: Public origin of the site, used by the Worker when it builds links back to a published record.

SITE_SUBDOMAIN.purpose: Subdomain for the GitHub Pages site.
SITE_SUBDOMAIN.whenUnset: Matches the Terraform default: the site is served from the apex, with A and AAAA records rather than a CNAME.

TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY.purpose: Public half of the contact form's Turnstile widget, inlined into the site bundle. Public by construction, which is why it is a variable and not a secret; its secret half is a Worker secret.
TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY.whenUnset: The contact page renders a notice instead of a form, because a form with no challenge is one the Worker would refuse anyway. The Pages workflow warns, because the two outcomes look identical until somebody tries to write.

TF_STATE_BUCKET.purpose: R2 bucket holding Terraform state, shared across projects and separated by state key prefix.

WORKER_BASE_URL.purpose: Public origin of the Worker. The media pipeline and the contact check post their callbacks there, and the site's contact form posts submissions to it.

WORKER_ENABLED.purpose: Whether Terraform attaches the Worker's custom domain.
WORKER_ENABLED.whenUnset: Falls back to false at the reference site. The domain cannot bind to a script that does not exist, so this stays off until Wrangler has deployed the Worker once.

WORKER_NAME.purpose: Wrangler service name of the Worker. generate-wrangler.ts refuses to build a configuration without it, and Terraform's custom domain routes to it by name.

CALLBACK_HMAC_SECRET.purpose: Shared between the Worker and the media pipeline, and the only reason the Worker believes a media-processed callback.

CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN.purpose: Write credential for Terraform apply and for Wrangler. R2, Workers Scripts, Turnstile, DNS, Cache Rules, Workers Routes, Zone and SSL.

CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN_PLAN.purpose: Read-only mirror of CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, used by the pull-request plan job. A job triggered by a branch must not hold a credential that can change infrastructure. See the README.

R2_MEDIA_RW_ACCESS_KEY_ID.purpose: S3 access key id for the public media bucket, write scope, used only by the media pipeline's upload step.

R2_PRIVATE_RO_ACCESS_KEY_ID.purpose: S3 access key id for the private bucket, read-only: the media pipeline reads originals and must never be able to destroy the only copy.

R2_STATE_RO_ACCESS_KEY_ID.purpose: S3 access key id for the Terraform state bucket, read-only, used by the pull-request plan job. terraform plan never persists state, so read is enough. See the README.

R2_STATE_RW_ACCESS_KEY_ID.purpose: S3 access key id for the Terraform state bucket, write scope, used only by the apply workflow.

TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USER_IDS.purpose: Comma-separated numeric Telegram ids allowed to author. Everything else is dropped without a reply.

TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN.purpose: BotFather token the Worker uses to answer Telegram.

TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET.purpose: Value Telegram was given at registration and sends back on every update; the Worker rejects anything without it.

TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY.purpose: Secret half of the contact form's Turnstile widget, synced to the Worker, which verifies every submission's token against it. Without it the Worker refuses every message.

WORKERS_AI_API_TOKEN.purpose: Runs the model that screens a contact message. Account -> Workers AI -> Read and nothing else: deliberately not CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, which can rewrite the buckets and the DNS.

WORKER_DISPATCH_TOKEN.purpose: Becomes the Worker's GITHUB_DISPATCH_TOKEN, which dispatches the media workflow. The names differ because GitHub reserves the GITHUB_ prefix and will not store a secret using it.
